note: Extra vetted names for later expansion. Not the 15 sample monsters. None of these names are reused there. High-sensitivity beings (worshipped figures, living sacred beings) are omitted. Protected character names from anime and games are omitted. A row marked medium still has a written distance. Concepts stay inside the sourced facts or the researcher's one-line pitch. They are not full monster records.

names.concept: A goose that files paperwork proving it hatched from a barnacle on a dock piling, because that is the story it was told.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Medieval misbelief about geese and barnacles. Not a branded bird.

names.concept: A snow-white bird in a king's hallway that looks at you, takes the illness into itself, and leaves with the lunch as well. The bestiary's later moral is not on the card.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Physiologus bird. No sacred-moral cartoon and no game phoenix.

names.concept: A sandy back with a little scrub on it that offers a picnic and then remembers it is the tide. The allegory that called it a devil stays in the research, not the joke.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Bestiary false-island whale or turtle. The picnic is new. No demonic branding.

names.concept: A buffalo-like beast whose head is too heavy to lift, so the dangerous look points at the floor and it apologizes into the dirt.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Classical beast. Not a video-game catoblepas model.

names.concept: A serpent king small enough to lose in a pocket, lethal in a glance, undone when someone walks past wearing a weasel's smell.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Pliny's small basilisk, not a game cockatrice costume. The weasel smell is the sourced weakness.

names.concept: A two-legged serpent with a rooster's head that still tries to announce dawn and start a barnyard duel.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Folklore hybrid. Distinct from Inchking: this one has the rooster head and the dawn habit.

names.concept: A human-faced lion that files the spines on its tail like a clerk's pens and hates a leftover on the page. The devouring is not the joke.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Persian-through-bestiary hybrid. Pens instead of a game manticore's missile volley as the whole identity.

names.thaiName: ค่าบังเหียน
names.concept: A grey loch horse that offers a ride and keeps the fare clamped in its teeth. If it looks like a person, the hooves are still in the shoes.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Scottish water horse. Not the Falkirk steel sculpture and not a game mount. Hooves-in-human-form is the sourced tell.

names.thaiName: ม้าข้อสัญญา
names.concept: The meaner water horse, distinct from Bitfare: there is no fare, only a contract, and the contract is the vicious part.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Folklore water horse kept separate from the kelpie on purpose. The prop is a contract, not a bridle receipt, so it is not a recolour.

names.thaiName: หัวใต้เบาะ
names.concept: A headless coachman who carries his own head and keeps setting it on the wrong seat. The source's confidence is medium; the card should say so.
names.ipSimilarityReason: The headless coach image is famous and, per the research record, poorly attested. Our joke is the misplaced head, not a film dullahan. Research confidence stays medium.

names.concept: A tiny squatter in a ruined tower whose cap will not rinse clean. The card does not show the killing the folklore tells. The stain is the whole identity.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Border folklore goblin. Laundry, not murder, is the joke. Not a game redcap's combat kit.

names.thaiName: สุนัขเคอร์ฟิว
names.concept: A cart-sized black dog that might be a death omen and might only want company at closing time. It is not staged in a churchyard, and the folklore name is not on the card.
names.ipSimilarityReason: East Anglian black dog. No church joke, no devil etymology as a gag, and not a hellhound franchise model.

names.concept: A polite lantern over a wet ditch that shows the path, waits until it is trusted, and then goes out.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Folklore fool's fire. Not a game wisp's spell effect.

names.concept: A German household spirit that does the chores and then invoices the kitchen in missing spoons. No candle on the head, no mine cart.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Folklore hausgeist. The candle-hat mine creature from a living game is a different design and is not used.

names.thaiName: เสมียนเนิน
names.concept: A burial-mound landlord who keeps haunting because the treasure inventory is unfinished. It is a clerk with a list, not a shouting armored corpse from a game.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Saga draugr as a mound guardian of treasure. The research record itself warns that the modern 'Norse zombie' look is a later reading.

names.concept: A seal-person whose skin is in the coat check under the wrong ticket. When the ticket is found, they leave. The stolen-marriage plot is not played as comedy.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Northern Isles selkie. The card is a lost-ticket problem. Coercion is not the joke.

names.concept: A luck spirit that arrives as whichever farm animal was not on the list, usually a goat when the form said horse.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Celtic shapechanger. Not a specific film pooka.

names.concept: A night helper who does the chores for a dish of milk and resigns forever if the thanks is the wrong size.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Scottish brownie. Not a film house-elf: no matching uniform, no big-eyed costume, just a hairy night shift and a milk bowl.

names.concept: A small blue flame that leads to the good ore and walks off if the pay packet is one coin over or one coin under.
names.ipSimilarityReason: English mine fairy. A union rule, not a will-o'-the-wisp recolour: this one cares about the exact wage.

names.concept: A slimy cavern snail-serpent whose hairy reach does all the hunting as one extremely committed hug. The slime on the floor arrives first.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Landes folklore beast. Not a game purple worm.

names.concept: A west-coast loch being whose usual form is a huge diver-bird and that also shows up as a water bull, then wonders which name to answer to.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Scottish shapeshifter. The bird-and-bull pair is the tell. The English folklore name is not used, because it sounds like a different joke.

names.thaiName: ฝูงแย่งที่
names.concept: A crescent of flying dead that lifts one person, carries them between landings, and then argues about who had the seat.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Irish and Scottish host of the dead. The seating argument is the new motive. Not a game wraith squadron.

names.thaiName: สัตว์คลุมเครือ
names.concept: A lake monster that cannot agree with its own sources whether it is a beaver, a crocodile, or something with a bill. It wears all three as a maybe.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Welsh lake monster with disagreeing descriptions. The indecision is the design, not a pick of one modern movie lake-beast.

names.concept: A water dragon whose entire kingdom is one serious puddle, and who still enters as if the puddle were a sea.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Sussex knuckerhole dragon. One puddle, not a world-serpent and not Duty Puddle the janitor spill.

names.concept: Lion, goat, and serpent sharing one torso and unable to agree whose turn it is to breathe. Flame, if drawn, is a picture, not an element.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Classical chimera body plan. Not a particular game model. Distinct from the Japanese nue entry, which is about sources that disagree.

names.thaiName: จ้องฉบับร่าง
names.concept: A winged critic with the archaic face: staring eyes, snake hair, a wide mouth, and tusks. Her glare files you as a statue of your worst draft. Not a film's beautiful gorgon.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Closest protected things are film and game Medusas. Distance is the archaic tusked round face from the fetched vase description, plus a critic's draft instead of a hero's shield.

names.concept: Three immortal one-eyed smiths who will not hand over a thunderbolt without a signed work order. The gods in the source story are not the punchline.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Hesiodic smiths, kept separate from the one-eyed shepherd. No film cyclops costume.

names.concept: A one-eyed shepherd who blocks the cave path and runs the place with a one-star mood. People are not on the menu. The famous blinding trick is not used, because the fetched page did not give it.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Homeric one-eyed shepherd. Not a game cyclops, and not a joke about eating guests.

names.thaiName: เพลงเสากระโดง
names.concept: A small choir with women's voices and birds' bodies, singing from a mast. No fish tail.
names.ipSimilarityReason: The fetched page shows bird-bodied sirens. A mermaid tail would collide with protected modern characters and is not used.

names.concept: A doorway with six long necks that taxes a passing group by taking one snack. The grisly teeth stay off the card; the count of necks is the tell.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Literary sea monster. Snack tax instead of a ship-eating scene. Not a game boss model.

names.concept: A whirlpool that inhales and gives the water back on the schedule already written in the old accounts. The card does not invent a new timer.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Homeric tide monster. The schedule is the sourced habit. Not a film maelstrom shot.

names.concept: Winged snatchers who take the plate and leave a polite crumb. The fouling in the old story is not the joke.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Wind daimones. Not the sirens, and not a game harpy's scream.

names.concept: A winged lion with a woman's face who will not let the landing proceed until the answer is in. She is the Theban plague-monster, not the Egyptian royal sphinx and not the Giza portrait.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Greek literary sphinx. Medium because the riddle-lion is immediately recognizable. Distance: no Giza body, no modern film sphinx, and the toll is an overdue answer.

names.concept: A three-headed gate hound in three porter jackets, one per shift, who lets people in and will not clock them out. Snake mane is a small tell, not a film collar.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Closest protected looks are film and game three-headed dogs. Distance: porter uniforms and a time-clock, no flaming eyes as a logo, no named hero's labour.

names.concept: A lion whose mane shrugs off a strike and only loses a grapple. No hero's costume and no club.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Labour beast. The rule is the hide. Not a particular illustrated Heracles scene.

names.concept: A bound wolf that bites the hand offered as a pledge. The chain is made of ridiculous ingredients from the story, including a cat's footstep and a fish's breath. No franchise wolf.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Medium cultural sensitivity: a monster inside a mythology some people hold as religious. The joke is the broken pledge and the silly fetter, not the faith. God of War and Marvel designs are off limits.

names.thaiName: ต่อแถวตัวเอง
names.concept: A serpent so long it has to queue behind its own tail. Big enough that a normal card may be the wrong size. Not a game boss's face.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Medium sensitivity for the same religious mythology as the pledge wolf. The queue is the joke. Marvel and game designs are not used.
names.suggestedCategory: later — ask Agent 07 before a boss use
names.scaleNote: Large. Agent 07 should see this before it becomes a world boss.

names.thaiName: เกล็ดเงินเดือน
names.concept: A paymaster who sits on the payroll until the gold turns him into the vault. No opera staging and no hero's cooking scene.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Saga dragon. Wagner's ring cycle is a separate dramatic version and is not copied.

names.thaiName: สายตาสินบน
names.concept: A cedar-mountain bouncer whose look is deadly and who hands over seven terrors one bribe at a time. The face is not a copy of a museum mask or a game hero.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Literary demon from a Sumerian poem. The museum calls its mask 'usually believed' to be him, so the art does not trace that object.

names.thaiName: สั้นพ้นป่า
names.concept: Tree-tall among the trees and grass-tall the moment he steps off the path. Missing brows and one ear if the portrait needs the sourced face. The joke is the height rule, not a people.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Living Slavic folklore, sensitivity medium in the research record. The size rule is the parody. No steppe-mascot gag.

names.concept: A warden at the end of the hall whose sword is a closing bell. Embers are a picture, not an element. He is contractually the one who ends the night.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Medium sensitivity: a giant in a religious mythology. Not Marvel's fire demon. The bell is the new prop. Flame stays art color.
names.suggestedCategory: later — ask Agent 07 before a boss use
names.scaleNote: End-of-the-world scale in the source. Agent 07 should see it before a world-boss use.

names.concept: An eagle-headed lion that guards a desk of gold badges and hates a one-eyed auditor reaching over the rope.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Classical griffin. Not a heraldic logo, not a game mount, and not the one-eyed smiths.

names.thaiName: กระโดดแข็ง
names.concept: A reanimated corpse that the films taught to hop and that would rather sprint. Our version is stiff because the archive tags are too tight. No official robes from a movie.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Chinese folklore corpse. The hop is flagged by the research as a cinema image. Tags-and-stiffness avoid copying that costume and avoid a joke about dress.

names.concept: A supernatural tanuki whose leaf is a bad receipt. Not Receiptfox: this one is the leaf, not a fox bewitching names. Named tanuki that receive rites are left alone.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Folklore bake-danuki. Medium in the research record because some named ones are ritual subjects. This card uses an unnamed trickster and a leaf.

names.concept: A customer whose body stays in line while the collar, and the neck inside it, reaches the back counter.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Yokai with a stretching neck. Not the flying-head type, so it is one joke, and not a manga face.

names.thaiName: กำแพงถัดไป
names.concept: An invisible wall too tall to climb and too wide to walk around, which is simply the next room refusing to load. Not the modern manga creature with a dog-like face.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Folklore invisible wall. Shigeru Mizuki's nurikabe is named by the research as a separate modern depiction and is not drawn.

names.thaiName: สำเนาป้องกัน
names.concept: A beaked, three-legged sea figure that prophesies a good harvest or a sick season and is answered by copying its picture. The art is original, not a trace of the 1846 print.
names.ipSimilarityReason: 1846 prophecy-beast. Copying the picture is the sourced defense. The card does not reproduce that woodblock.

names.concept: A beast sewn from the spare pieces of other animals that eats the party's bad dreams and, occasionally, a good one. It is not drawn as a modern tapir.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Folklore dream-eater. The research separates that from the tapir, which is only the modern animal sense of the word.

names.concept: A nocturnal chimera whose own bestiaries cannot agree which animal donated which part, so it argues with itself inside a small black cloud. Not Turnshare, which is one body taking turns.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Heike nue. The disagreement between sources is the sourced fact. Not a game chimera and not the Greek one.

names.thaiName: ค่าข้ามน้ำ
names.concept: A hornless scaled river dragon that charges a toll to cross its gutter. The old tattoo ward is not a joke.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Chinese aquatic dragon, low sensitivity in the research record. Distinct from sacred long dragons, which that record says not to parody.

names.thaiName: หน้ายังไม่ขึ้น
names.concept: A help-desk clerk who looks human until the face fails to load. You stop asking, and the next clerk is blank too.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Faceless yokai. Not a creepypasta tall man, and not a copy of one illustrated story's street. The double blank is the folklore scare, restaged as a desk.

names.concept: An umbrella ghost that opens indoors on purpose. No single eye, no single leg, and no licking tongue, because the research pass did not find those in the English lead.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Umbrella yokai. The missing eye-and-leg details are deliberately not invented.

names.thaiName: ลมกระดาษบาด
names.concept: A weasel in a dust devil that leaves a papercut which does not hurt, then apologizes as if the form required it.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Regional yokai. The painless cut is sourced. The apology is the comedy. Not a storm god.

names.nameOwnershipNote: OWNER_DECIDED t282u: first proposer keeps the name. names.thaiName: อ่างวิจารณ์
names.concept: A bathroom critic with a clipboard who only stays while there is grime to grade, and who will not fight a clean tub. The licking is not the picture.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Edo yokai of bath filth. The card is a critic and a clean-tub weakness, not a gross-out.

names.thaiName: เสมียนเขี้ยว
names.concept: A small leathery household goblin who keeps the incident ledger and bites the corner of any form that is late. Green skin is not required.
names.ipSimilarityReason: European folklore goblin. Not a green game goblin and not the murderous end of the stories. Agent 01 had not published an RPG goblin.

names.concept: A sun-bird that bows, goes up in ash, and comes back as a sooty hen still wearing the bow tie. The next bow is already starting.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Greek phoenix motif of rising from ashes. Not a game summon and not an Egyptian sacred-bird costume.

names.concept: A tall cloaked leaper with metallic claws who clears a queue in one jump and then asks which bus. The flames in the reports are not the attack.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Victorian urban legend. Leaps and claws are sourced. Not one penny-dreadful plate copied whole, and not a superhero.

names.thaiName: หินคนเดียว
names.concept: A troll whose family unit is one and whose address is a rock. The fetched page does not mention a bridge toll, so there isn't one.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Old Norse rock-dweller. No bridge, no game troll regen.

names.concept: A kangaroo-odd hopper with a goat's head, bat wings, and cloven hooves, lost in a service corridor and screaming because the signage is wrong. The folklore name's religious word is not on the card.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Pine Barrens cryptid. Wings, hooves, and the odd head are the tell. No devil joke.

names.concept: A yeoman archer in a faded green tabard who robbed the rich, got the grocery bag, and is trying to give it back.
names.ipSimilarityReason: English outlaw legend. Not a film's tights-and-feather costume. The give-back is the twist on the sourced reputation.

names.concept: A barn owl on a branch whose shadow was written up as a monster, and the shadow has filed a complaint.
names.ipSimilarityReason: 1952 report plus the later barn-owl explanation. Not a copy of a famous flying-saucer illustration's head.

names.concept: A toxic little root shaped like a person that resents being a remedy. It does not scream. The fetched page never said it did.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Mediterranean plant lore. The screaming root is a later fiction image and is excluded.

names.thaiName: จิ้มจานรอง
names.concept: A small auditor that only visits unattended livestock drinks and leaves a neat puncture in the saucer. Not a reptile with spines, not a hairless dog, and not the film creature the research says one witness description matched.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Americas cryptid. Medium because the goat-sucker story is specific and one witness account was linked to the creature Sil in the film Species. This design is a saucer and a clipboard.

names.thaiName: เถียงในห้องขับ
names.concept: A cockpit with two arguments and no famous robot outside it: one voice wants a shouting miracle, the other is reading the fuel gauge.
names.ipSimilarityReason: The genre split is usable. Mazinger Z and Gundam are named in the research as the markers and are not drawn. Medium because a giant robot still points at those machines.

names.thaiName: โบว์เบี้ยว
names.concept: A transformation that cannot begin until a ribbon bow is even. No sailor collar, no wand from a show, no makeup sequence copied from a series.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Genre pattern. Medium because 1990s transforming-hero shows own the famous version. The only prop is a crooked bow.

names.thaiName: ชื่อในกระจก
names.concept: A dim mirror that will not let you pass until your badge name is said the way it is printed. It critiques pronunciation. It does not teach a chant, and it does not name a historical queen.
names.ipSimilarityReason: Mirror folklore. Medium because the ritual is living folklore and one proposed origin is a historical monarch. Neither the ritual steps nor that monarch are used.
